title: College Football Matchup at Lambeau Field
seoTitle: Notre Dame vs. Wisconsin College Football at Lambeau
subtitle: The Notre Dame vs. Wisconsin game promises excitement and extensive logistics
excerpt: Notre Dame and Wisconsin face off in a college football game at Lambeau Field in Green Bay this Sunday.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
This Sunday, Lambeau Field will host the college football game between Notre Dame and Wisconsin, part of the Shamrock Series. The game, set for 6:30 PM CT, is drawing fans from both sides and features a range of services and activities prepared for the day.

Tickets and Parking

Tickets have already been sold and distributed by each university. For those who haven't secured theirs, the last available tickets can be purchased at Ticketmaster.com. Mobile parking pass holders must have their pass ready on their phone when entering lots starting at 2:30 PM CT, with stadium gates opening at 4:30 PM CT. Most stadium parking is already sold out; any remaining passes can be purchased via Ticketmaster. Those without mobile parking passes can utilize neighborhood parking, adhering to local regulations. Paid parking options are also available at nearby residences and businesses. Accessible parking for individuals with disabilities is provided in Lots 4 and 7, costing $80 (credit or debit card only) and requiring an ADA license plate or placard.

Stadium Atmosphere and Services

Lambeau Field's food and beverage concessions, including alcohol sales, will operate as they would for a regular game. The Atrium, home to the Packers Pro Shop, Hall of Fame, and 1919 Kitchen & Tap, will be open during regular business hours until Saturday evening, when it will close for a private event. On game day, Atrium access opens at 12:30 PM CT, allowing fans to enter and exit until 2:30 PM CT by scanning their ticket at the same door. Titletown Park offers free activities, including a DJ, field games, a beer garden, and mascot appearances. The “Titletown Gameday Live” event kicks off at 2:30 PM CT with live music, food, beverages, and games for all ages.

Security and Bag Policy

Standard game day security policies will be in effect. Fans may bring one clear bag no larger than 12" x 6" x 12", or a one-gallon clear plastic freezer bag. Small clutch purses, up to 4.5" x 6.5", are also permitted. Prohibited items include weapons, backpacks, coolers, strollers, umbrellas, large bags, selfie sticks, cameras with lenses exceeding 12 inches, and other restricted objects. Stadium parking is restricted to those with mobile parking passes, while Titletown parking is free on Saturday and available on a first-come, first-served basis.

Entertainment and Bands

Prior to the game, the Band of the Fighting Irish will perform on the field, and both university bands will present their shows at halftime. Following the game, both bands will play their respective alma maters. Wisconsin will not perform a "fifth quarter" show. The new “6 Degrees of Curly Lambeau” exhibit in the Hall of Fame highlights the connections between Notre Dame and Wisconsin.

Accessibility and Support Services

The stadium provides hearing assistance and accessibility services, including hearing devices, noise-canceling headphones, and sensory bags. Additionally, a dedicated alcohol-free zone is available in Section 112, along with a lost person prevention program. Families can utilize restrooms and lactation rooms located throughout the stadium. For guests without credit/debit cards, cash-to-card conversion stations are available in the Atrium.

Broadcast and Coverage

For those unable to attend, the game will be broadcast nationwide on NBC at 6:30 PM CT. Further information and updates are available on the packers.com/Lambeau-field/NDvsWisconsin website.

Information provided by Green Bay Packers.
